newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet extends gain, fuel oil up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet extends gain, fuel oil up.

text.p: Singapore front month jet fuel swaps extended its early day gains late afternoon Thursday on scarce prompt physical availabilties while fuel oil firmed on buying from cracker players, traders said.
"The February regrade (jet fuel/gas oil swap spread) is widening because of the large physical spread between the two products," one trader said.
February regrade was last quoted at $3.80/$4.00 per barrel up sharply from Wednesday's $3.30 buying number, brokers said.
The big jump, brokers said was due to the large spread between physical jet fuel and gas oil currently at a hefty $5.00 per barrel.
On Wednesday, 150,000 barrels of physical gas oil traded at $25.20 per barrel while 100,000 barrels of jet fuel traded at $30.40 per barrel, both on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
March regrade swaps edged up slightly reflecting a bigger squeeze on prompt cargoes with the further out months looking more balanced, traders said.
The market was last quoted at $2.15/$3.35 per barrel against Wednesday's $2.00/$2.20, brokers said. It traded earlier today at $2.15, they said.

Gas oil swaps was unchanged from the morning in quiet trading but was firmer than Wednesday due to stronger overnight crude values where February Brent crude closed up 52 cents to $22.77 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $25.80/$26.00 per barrel from Wednesday's $25.55/$25.75.
Fuel oil swaps rose on buying from players who were looking to capture the fuel oil and Dubai crack spread at around the $4.00 per tonne mark.
Brokers said deals were done at $100.00, $100.25 and $100.50 some of which were tied to crack spreads.
Front month Singapore fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $100.00/$101.00 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $99.00/$99.50, brokers said.
Naphtha rose sharply in line with the 52-cent hike to crude values with February quoted at $24.00/$24.20 per barrel from Wednesday's $23.40/$23.70 per barrel, one broker said.
